strategy.summary: Trade the dollar's daily swing around the 4 pm London FX fix, daytime only. Krohn, Mueller & Whelan (Journal of Finance, 2024) find the US dollar rises into the big FX fixes and falls after them, a W shape around the clock, which they tie to dealers hedging predictable fix orders. After costs the post-London reversal held up through 2019 while the Tokyo legs faded. 6E is quoted in dollars per euro, so going long 6E is short the dollar. Only the two daytime windows are tested; the overnight Tokyo and pre-ECB legs are left out on purpose.
strategy.formula: pre leg: short 6E from the ECB fix (14:15 Frankfurt) to the London fix (16:00 London); post leg: long 6E from the London fix

rules.label: Clock
rules.text: Each fix is set in its own time zone and converted to New York time every day: London 16:00 is 11:00 ET most weeks and 12:00 ET in the weeks when only the US is on summer time; the ECB fix is 08:15 ET (09:15 in those weeks). The switch time is the London fix plus -15 min, -5 min, at fix, +5 min or +15 min.

rules.label: Enter
rules.text: At the open of the first 1-minute bar at or after the leg's start time (skipped if that bar is more than 5 minutes late). Pre leg: short at the ECB fix. Post leg: long at the switch time. Both: the pre trade, then the post trade. Optional vol gate: only trade when the 20-day average daily realized volatility is above (high) or at/below (low) its 250-day median, known before the day starts.

rules.label: Exit
rules.text: Pre leg: at the switch time. Post leg: after 60 min, 120 min or 240 min, or at 17:00 ET. Exits fill at the close of the last bar before the exit time. Optional stop 0.25% or 0.5% from the entry, live inside each bar.

rules.label: Size
rules.text: One position at a time, never held overnight (only bars from 08:00 to 17:00 ET are used). As many whole 6E contracts as the account covers at full contract value (no leverage), starting from $1,000,000.

strategy.grid_text: Every combination was tested: 405 versions. The post-fix and both-legs settings use every value of every axis; the pre-fix leg has no post-fix hold, so it gets one version per switch time, vol gate and stop.
strategy.length_note: Times are minutes on the New York clock relative to the day's London fix; the stop is a percent of the entry price. The pre leg ignores the post-fix hold.

funnel.name: Start
funnel.why: All 405 versions backtested once on 2018–2022 data.

funnel.name: 1 · Integrity
funnel.why: Per-trade checks on every version: the fix times (in London and Frankfurt time) and the vol gate were recomputed independently, each trade entered at its leg's start time on the right side, no planned trade was skipped, fills were never better than the market, every bar was inside 08:00–17:00 ET of one day (nothing held overnight). Plus 40 random versions re-run on cut-off data. 0 failed.

funnel.name: 2 · Enough trades
funnel.why: Needs ≥100 completed trades and ≥10 a year in ≥4 of the 5 years. Removed 135 (135 on 1min).

funnel.name: 3 · Profit
funnel.why: Needs a net profit, Sharpe ≥ 0.75 and drawdown no worse than 30%. Removed 270 (270 on 1min); 270 of them lost money.

funnel.name: 4 · Stable settings
funnel.why: Each setting is nudged one at a time, down and up: the switch time by ±5 minutes, a timed post-fix hold by ±30 minutes and a stop by ±0.1% ("to 17:00" and "no stop" have nothing to nudge). At least 70% of the nudged versions must be profitable, with median Sharpe ≥ 0.5. Removed 0.

funnel.name: 6 · Remove duplicates
funnel.why: Versions whose monthly returns correlate ≥ 0.8 form a group; the best 2 of each go on (a group of one keeps its one). 0 versions formed 0 groups; 0 of the 0 picks are distinct backtests.

funnel.name: 8 · Validation
funnel.why: Frozen finalists run once on unseen data: needs net > 0, Sharpe ≥ 0.3, drawdown no worse than 30% and ≥40 trades.

luck.method: Per bar size and leg setting (post = long only, pre = short only, both = the finalists' actual long share): random intraday trades on random sessions at random times, never overlapping and always closed by the session's last bar, covering the target share of the validation window's bars. Trade lengths are drawn from that group's own validation trades; each trade is long with the group's actual long share (1.0 for long-only, 0.0 for short-only), else short. Same fills, slippage, commission and whole-contract sizing as the strategy; scored with the same daily-Sharpe and time-in-market code.
luck.text: For every whole-percent time in market in each group's 2023–2024 range, 100 random runs trade 6E at random times of the 08:00–17:00 ET day on random days, so they test whether the fix times matter. Each group is one leg setting. Like the strategy, the random trades are intraday only, never overlap, and are always closed by the session's last bar. Their lengths are drawn from that group's own finalist trades, so trade counts and costs match. Post-fix groups trade long and pre-fix groups short; "both" groups go long with the same share of trades their finalists did. They pay the same costs and use the same sizing and Sharpe math as the strategy.

assumptions: Data: Databento CME continuous front month (6E.v.0), 1-minute bars from 08:00 to 17:00 ET (not the 08:20–15:00 pit session the other 6E pages use, because the post-London window runs to 17:00). Rolls are back-adjusted and happen at 00:00 UTC, so no trade crosses one.
Costs: 1 tick slippage per side (stops too) and $2.50 commission per contract per side.

The paper used spot rates from 1999 to 2019 and charged half the quoted spot spread; it reports the same pattern in CME futures from 2006. Nothing after 2019 was in the paper, so 2018–2026 here is partly new.
The pre-London leg had no clear sign in the paper; it is tested as the exploratory half of the W.
The transfer check runs the same rules on 6J. The paper finds the yen moves the other way after London, so a good yen result is a warning sign, not support.
Each trade uses the whole account in whole contracts with no leverage, the same as the other families; the stop changes where the trade exits, not how big it is.
Sharpe uses daily mark-to-market returns (√252), with idle cash earning 0%. Time in market is the share of 1-minute bars with an open position.
Other strategy families were already selected on this market's 2023–2024 data, so 2023–2024 is not untouched; only the 2025+ holdout is.
Holdout (2025 onward) has not been run. It is a one-time final test and needs an explicit go-ahead.
